The ugliness of this is well known by nature and by intellects, and the Law of the Most Wise of Judges is exalted above bringing it.

(Section)

Many ignorant people have thought that fornication with a slave is like something permissible, or permissible, or that it is easier than committing it with a free person. This group has interpreted the Qur'an in support of this and included the slave in His saying: ﴿except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy.﴾

Some women have even allowed their male slave access to themselves, interpreting the Qur'an in that way. Thus a woman who had married her slave was brought before 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and she interpreted this verse; so 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) separated them, disciplined her, and said, "Woe to you! This is only for men, not for women."

Whoever interprets this verse as permitting intercourse with male slaves is a disbeliever by the consensus of the Ummah. Our shaykh said: Among these are some who interpret His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And a believing slave is better than an idolater, even though he pleases you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221] in that way. He said: Some people asked me about this verse, and he was one who recited the Qur'an, and he thought its meaning was the permissibility of believing male slaves.

He said: Among them are those who make it a matter of disagreement, which some scholars permit and others forbid, and they say: their disagreement is a doubt. This is a lie and ignorance, for there is no sect of the Ummah that permits it, nor any religion of the messengers. It is permitted only by the heretics of the world who do not believe in Allah, His messengers, His books, and the Last Day.

He said: Among them are those who say: it is permissible in cases of necessity, such as a man remaining forty days without intercourse, and similar matters about which groups of soldiers, common people, and the poor have addressed and questioned me.

He said: Among them are those who have heard of some scholars' disagreement about the obligation of the hadd penalty for it, and so thought that this was a disagreement about its prohibition, not knowing that a thing may be among the gravest prohibitions, like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine, and yet have no prescribed penalty.

Then that disagreement may be a weak opinion, and from that weak opinion, which is an error of some mujtahids, and this corrupt assumption which is the error of some ignorant people, arises the alteration of religion, obedience to Satan, and disobedience to the Lord of the Worlds. When false opinions are joined to false assumptions, and overpowering desires assist them, then do not ask about the alteration of religion thereafter and the complete departure from the whole of the laws.

When this matter became easy in the souls of many people, many slaves began to boast that they know none but their master, that no one else has had intercourse with them, just as a female slave or wife boasts that she knows none but her master or husband. Likewise many beardless youths boast that they know none but their companion, friend, brother, or teacher. Likewise among the active partners, one boasts of being chaste regarding anyone other than his companion who is his peer and associate like a wife, or other than his male slave who is like his concubine.

Among them are those who consider that prohibition applies only to coercing a boy into committing the abomination; so if he is willing and consenting, there is no harm in it. It seems that for them what is forbidden is only the injustice and aggression of coercing the one acted upon.

The shaykh said: One trustworthy person related to me that one of these was seized for this abomination and was sentenced to the hadd penalty, and he said: "By Allah, he consented to it, and I did not coerce or force him, so how am I to be punished?" Then the supporter of the polytheists, who was present, said: "This is the judgment of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, and these people are not at fault."

Among them are those who believe that if passion for a beloved reaches the point where the lover fears destruction, intercourse with the beloved becomes permissible for him out of necessity and preservation of the soul, just as carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine become permissible in extreme hunger.

These people may also permit drinking wine for the purpose of treatment and preserving health, if it is free from the disgrace of intoxication.

There is no doubt that disbelief, wickedness, and sins are of degrees, just as faith and righteous deeds are of degrees, as Allah says: ﴿They are of various ranks with Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ [Al 'Imran: 163], and He says: ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ [al-An'am: 132]. And He says: ﴿The postponement is only an increase in disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 37], and He says: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. And as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has added to their wavering, filth upon their filth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124–125]. Its parallels in the Qur'an are numerous.

Among the lightest of these in offense is one who commits it while believing it to be prohibited, and when he has satisfied his need he says: "I seek Allah's forgiveness," as if what had happened had never happened.

Satan has thus toyed with most of this creation, as children toy with a ball, and has brought forth for them all kinds of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience in every mold.

In sum, the grades of fornication vary according to their corruptions. One who takes a regular female companion, or a woman who takes a regular male companion, is less evil than one who fornicates with everyone. One who conceals what he commits is less sinful than the open flaunter who publicizes it, and one who keeps it secret is less sinful than the one who informs people of it and talks about it. The flaunter is far from Allah's well-being and pardon, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"All my nation will be pardoned except those who openly sin, and it is part of open sinning that a man commits a sin at night, and Allah conceals it for him, then in the morning he says, 'O so-and-so, last night I did such-and-such,' while his Lord had concealed it, and in the morning he uncovers what Allah had concealed of himself."

Or as he said.

In another hadith from him (ﷺ): "Whoever is afflicted with something of these filthy things, let him conceal himself with Allah's concealment, for whoever reveals to us his face, We will bring upon him the Book of Allah." In another hadith: "Indeed, when a sin is hidden, it harms none but its doer; but when it is made public and is not denounced, it harms the common people."

Likewise, fornication with a woman who has no husband is less sinful than fornication with a married woman, because of the injustice and aggression against the husband it involves, and corrupting his bed. The sin of the former may be greater than the sin of mere fornication, or less.

Fornication with the wife of a neighbor is graver in sin than fornication with a distant woman, because of the harm to the neighbor that accompanies it and the failure to observe the command of Allah and His Messenger concerning him.

Likewise, fornication with the wife of one who fights in the way of Allah is graver in sin before Allah than fornication with another. For this reason, on the Day of Resurrection he will be made to stand, and it will be said to him: "Take from his good deeds what you wish."

Just as its degrees vary according to the one fornicated with, so its degrees vary according to time, place, and circumstances, and according to the doer.

Fornication in Ramadan, by night or by day, is graver in sin than in other times. Likewise, in the noble and virtuous places it is graver in sin than elsewhere.

As for its variation according to the doer: fornication by a free person is more heinous than by a slave. For this reason his penalty is half of the penalty for the free.

Fornication by a married person is more heinous than by an unmarried one, and by an elderly person more heinous than by a young one.

For this reason, among the three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify, and for whom there is a painful punishment, is the elderly adulterer. Fornication by a scholar is more heinous than by an ignorant person, because of his knowledge of its ugliness and its consequences, and his committing it with insight. Fornication by one able to do without it is more heinous than by a poor, incapable person.

(Section)

If a man is able to marry or take a concubine, the practice of masturbation with his hand is forbidden to him.

Ibn 'Aqil said: "Our companions and our shaykh mentioned nothing but disliking it; they did not state it as prohibited."

He said: "If he cannot find a wife or concubine, and has no desire that would drive him to fornication, masturbation is forbidden to him, because it is enjoyment of oneself, and the verse prevents it. If his condition is wavering between lethargy and desire, and he has no wife while he has a female slave, and does not marry, it is disliked but not forbidden. If he is overpowered by his desire and fears severe hardship, like a captive, a traveler, or a poor man, it is permissible for him, as Ahmad (may Allah be pleased with him) stated explicitly."

It is related that the Companions used to do it during their campaigns and journeys. If a woman without a husband has intense desire, some of our companions said: it is permissible for her to use the "ukranbaj," which is something made of leather in the shape of a male organ, which she inserts, or something similar, such as small cucumbers or gourds.

The correct view in my opinion is that this is not permitted, because the Prophet (ﷺ) only directed the one with desire who is unable to marry to fasting; and if there were another meaning, he would have mentioned it. And if he is absent from her, since the act is permissible and one who imagines and fantasizes about it is not forbidden. But if it is a boy or a stranger, it is disliked for him, since it is an incitement of his soul to the forbidden and an urging of her toward it. And if he hollows out a melon, or dough, or a leather piece, or a idol's niche, and penetrates it, then the detail we have mentioned applies.

I say: This is easier than his masturbating with his hand.

Ahmad has said regarding one who has a strong desire for intercourse, unable to control himself, and fears his testicles might rupture: he should feed [the poor]. This is the wording quoted from him in al-Mughni; then he said: "He permitted him to break the fast because he fears for himself, so he is like the sick person who fears death from thirst or the like, and he required feeding as a substitute for fasting. This is understood to apply to one who does not hope to be able to make up the fast. If he hopes for that, there is no expiation upon him, and the obligation is to wait for making up the fast and to do it when able, by His saying: ﴿And whoever among you is sick﴾ (the verse).

Recourse to expiation is only when despairing of making up the fast. If he feeds while despairing, and then becomes able to fast, it is possible that it is not required of him, since his obligation has been discharged by the expiation which was the obligation, and so he is not returned to the burden of what he has been freed from. It is also possible that making up the fast is required of him, since feeding is a substitute for despair, and we have shown that the despair has gone, so it is like the woman whose waiting period is by months, if she menstruates in the midst of it because of despair."

In the Fusul it is related from Ahmad about a man who feared that his bladder might burst from intense desire, or that his testicles might rupture from retaining water during Ramadan, that he should extract the water, and it does not mention with what he extracts it.

He said: "In my view, he extracts it by means that do not invalidate the fast of another, such as masturbating with his hand, or with the body of his wife or female slave who is not fasting. If he has a little girl slave or a young one, he may masturbate with her hand, and likewise with a non-Muslim woman.

It is permissible to have intercourse with her outside the private part. If he wishes to have intercourse in the private part while it is possible to extract the water by other means, then in my view it is not permitted, because when necessity is removed, what is beyond it remains forbidden, like satiety with carrion. Rather, here it is even more binding, since the matter of private parts is more strictly forbidden than eating."

I say: The apparent meaning of Ahmad's words is permissibility of intercourse, since he permitted breaking the fast and feeding. But if something like this occurred during menstruation, it would not be permitted for him to have intercourse, by unanimous agreement. So if it happened to a muhrim, he would extract his water and it would not be permitted for him to have intercourse.

(Section)

If the desire of the fasting person persists throughout the whole time, the making-up of the fast is dropped and he moves to expiation, like the old man and the old woman. If it recurs in summer or winter, he makes up the fast in the other season, and there is no expiation here, because it is a non-persistent excuse, so he is like the sick person. This is what is mentioned in the Fusul.

If his condition is wavering between lethargy and desire, and he has no wife while he has a female slave, and does not marry, it is disliked but not forbidden. If he is overpowered by his desire and fears severe hardship, like a captive, a traveler, or a poor man, it is permissible for him, as Ahmad (may Allah be pleased with him) stated explicitly."

It is related that the Companions used to do it during their campaigns and journeys. If a woman without a husband has intense desire, some of our companions said: it is permissible for her to use the "ukranbaj," which is something made of leather in the shape of a male organ, which she inserts, or something similar, such as small cucumbers or gourds.

The correct view in my opinion is that this is not permitted, because the Prophet (ﷺ) only directed the one with desire who is unable to marry to fasting; and if there were another meaning, he would have mentioned it. And if he is absent from her, since the act is permissible and one who imagines and fantasizes about it is not forbidden. But if it is a boy or a stranger, it is disliked for him, since it is an incitement of his soul to the forbidden and an urging of her toward it. And if he hollows out a melon, or dough, or a leather piece, or a idol's niche, and penetrates it, then the detail we have mentioned applies.

I say: This is easier than his masturbating with his hand.

Ahmad has said regarding one who has a strong desire for intercourse, unable to control himself, and fears his testicles might rupture: he should feed [the poor]. This is the wording quoted from him in al-Mughni; then he said: "He permitted him to break the fast because he fears for himself, so he is like the sick person who fears death from thirst or the like, and he required feeding as a substitute for fasting. This is understood to apply to one who does not hope to be able to make up the fast. If he hopes for that, there is no expiation upon him, and the obligation is to wait for making up the fast and to do it when able, by His saying: ﴿And whoever among you is sick﴾ (the verse).

Recourse to expiation is only when despairing of making up the fast. If he feeds while despairing, and then becomes able to fast, it is possible that it is not required of him, since his obligation has been discharged by the expiation which was the obligation, and so he is not returned to the burden of what he has been freed from. It is also possible that making up the fast is required of him, since feeding is a substitute for despair, and we have shown that the despair has gone, so it is like the woman whose waiting period is by months, if she menstruates in the midst of it because of despair."

In the Fusul it is related from Ahmad about a man who feared that his bladder might burst from intense desire, or that his testicles might rupture from retaining water during Ramadan, that he should extract the water, and it does not mention with what he extracts it.

He said: "In my view, he extracts it by means that do not invalidate the fast of another, such as masturbating with his hand, or with the body of his wife or female slave who is not fasting. If he has a little girl slave or a young one, he may masturbate with her hand, and likewise with a non-Muslim woman.

It is permissible to have intercourse with her outside the private part. If he wishes to have intercourse in the private part while it is possible to extract the water by other means, then in my view it is not permitted, because when necessity is removed, what is beyond it remains forbidden, like satiety with carrion. Rather, here it is even more binding, since the matter of private parts is more strictly forbidden than eating."

I say: The apparent meaning of Ahmad's words is permissibility of intercourse, since he permitted breaking the fast and feeding. But if something like this occurred during menstruation, it would not be permitted for him to have intercourse, by unanimous agreement. So if it happened to a muhrim, he would extract his water and it would not be permitted for him to have intercourse.

(Section)

If the desire of the fasting person persists throughout the whole time, the making-up of the fast is dropped and he moves to expiation, like the old man and the old woman. If it recurs in summer or winter, he makes up the fast in the other season, and there is no expiation here, because it is a non-persistent excuse, so he is like the sick person. This is what is mentioned in the Fusul.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 23, verse 5–7:

He (glorified is He) made the success of the servant contingent upon guarding his private parts from [unlawful use], so there is no path to success without it. He said: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers, who are humble in their prayer, who turn away from ill speech, who are active in giving zakat, who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1–7] up to His saying.

This contains three matters: that whoever does not guard his private parts is not among the successful, that he is among the blameworthy, and that he is among the transgressors. Thus he loses success, deserves the name of aggression, and falls into blame. The suffering of the pain of desire and its struggle is easier than some of that.

[Section: The wisdom in permitting the master to enjoy his female slave but not permitting the slave to enjoy his mistress]

As for his statement: "He permitted the man to enjoy his female slave by right of ownership, by intercourse and otherwise, and did not permit the woman to enjoy her slave, neither by intercourse nor otherwise," this too is part of the perfection and wisdom of this Law. The master dominates his slave, rules over him, and owns him, and the husband dominates his wife and rules over her, while she is under his authority and rule, like a captive. For this reason He prohibited the slave from marrying his mistress, because of the incompatibility between his being her slave and her husband, and between her being his mistress and the one he has intercourse with. The ugliness of this is well known by nature and by intellects, and the Law of the Most Wise of Judges is exalted above bringing it.

(Section)

Many ignorant people have thought that fornication with a slave is like something permissible, or permissible, or that it is easier than committing it with a free person. This group has interpreted the Qur'an in support of this and included the slave in His saying: ﴿except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy.﴾

Some women have even allowed their male slave access to themselves, interpreting the Qur'an in that way. Thus a woman who had married her slave was brought before 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and she interpreted this verse; so 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) separated them, disciplined her, and said, "Woe to you! This is only for men, not for women."

Whoever interprets this verse as permitting intercourse with male slaves is a disbeliever by the consensus of the Ummah. Our shaykh said: Among these are some who interpret His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And a believing slave is better than an idolater, even though he pleases you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221] in that way. He said: Some people asked me about this verse, and he was one who recited the Qur'an, and he thought its meaning was the permissibility of believing male slaves.

He said: Among them are those who make it a matter of disagreement, which some scholars permit and others forbid, and they say: their disagreement is a doubt. This is a lie and ignorance, for there is no sect of the Ummah that permits it, nor any religion of the messengers. It is permitted only by the heretics of the world who do not believe in Allah, His messengers, His books, and the Last Day.

He said: Among them are those who say: it is permissible in cases of necessity, such as a man remaining forty days without intercourse, and similar matters about which groups of soldiers, common people, and the poor have addressed and questioned me.

He said: Among them are those who have heard of some scholars' disagreement about the obligation of the hadd penalty for it, and so thought that this was a disagreement about its prohibition, not knowing that a thing may be among the gravest prohibitions, like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine, and yet have no prescribed penalty.

Then that disagreement may be a weak opinion, and from that weak opinion, which is an error of some mujtahids, and this corrupt assumption which is the error of some ignorant people, arises the alteration of religion, obedience to Satan, and disobedience to the Lord of the Worlds. When false opinions are joined to false assumptions, and overpowering desires assist them, then do not ask about the alteration of religion thereafter and the complete departure from the whole of the laws.

When this matter became easy in the souls of many people, many slaves began to boast that they know none but their master, that no one else has had intercourse with them, just as a female slave or wife boasts that she knows none but her master or husband. Likewise many beardless youths boast that they know none but their companion, friend, brother, or teacher. Likewise among the active partners, one boasts of being chaste regarding anyone other than his companion who is his peer and associate like a wife, or other than his male slave who is like his concubine.

Among them are those who consider that prohibition applies only to coercing a boy into committing the abomination; so if he is willing and consenting, there is no harm in it. It seems that for them what is forbidden is only the injustice and aggression of coercing the one acted upon.

The shaykh said: One trustworthy person related to me that one of these was seized for this abomination and was sentenced to the hadd penalty, and he said: "By Allah, he consented to it, and I did not coerce or force him, so how am I to be punished?" Then the supporter of the polytheists, who was present, said: "This is the judgment of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, and these people are not at fault."

Among them are those who believe that if passion for a beloved reaches the point where the lover fears destruction, intercourse with the beloved becomes permissible for him out of necessity and preservation of the soul, just as carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine become permissible in extreme hunger.

These people may also permit drinking wine for the purpose of treatment and preserving health, if it is free from the disgrace of intoxication.

There is no doubt that disbelief, wickedness, and sins are of degrees, just as faith and righteous deeds are of degrees, as Allah says: ﴿They are of various ranks with Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ [Al 'Imran: 163], and He says: ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ [al-An'am: 132]. And He says: ﴿The postponement is only an increase in disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 37], and He says: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. And as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has added to their wavering, filth upon their filth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124–125]. Its parallels in the Qur'an are numerous.

Among the lightest of these in offense is one who commits it while believing it to be prohibited, and when he has satisfied his need he says: "I seek Allah's forgiveness," as if what had happened had never happened.

Satan has thus toyed with most of this creation, as children toy with a ball, and has brought forth for them all kinds of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience in every mold.

In sum, the grades of fornication vary according to their corruptions. One who takes a regular female companion, or a woman who takes a regular male companion, is less evil than one who fornicates with everyone. One who conceals what he commits is less sinful than the open flaunter who publicizes it, and one who keeps it secret is less sinful than the one who informs people of it and talks about it. The flaunter is far from Allah's well-being and pardon, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"All my nation will be pardoned except those who openly sin, and it is part of open sinning that a man commits a sin at night, and Allah conceals it for him, then in the morning he says, 'O so-and-so, last night I did such-and-such,' while his Lord had concealed it, and in the morning he uncovers what Allah had concealed of himself."

Or as he said.

In another hadith from him (ﷺ): "Whoever is afflicted with something of these filthy things, let him conceal himself with Allah's concealment, for whoever reveals to us his face, We will bring upon him the Book of Allah." In another hadith: "Indeed, when a sin is hidden, it harms none but its doer; but when it is made public and is not denounced, it harms the common people."

Likewise, fornication with a woman who has no husband is less sinful than fornication with a married woman, because of the injustice and aggression against the husband it involves, and corrupting his bed. The sin of the former may be greater than the sin of mere fornication, or less.

Fornication with the wife of a neighbor is graver in sin than fornication with a distant woman, because of the harm to the neighbor that accompanies it and the failure to observe the command of Allah and His Messenger concerning him.

Likewise, fornication with the wife of one who fights in the way of Allah is graver in sin before Allah than fornication with another. For this reason, on the Day of Resurrection he will be made to stand, and it will be said to him: "Take from his good deeds what you wish."

Just as its degrees vary according to the one fornicated with, so its degrees vary according to time, place, and circumstances, and according to the doer.

Fornication in Ramadan, by night or by day, is graver in sin than in other times. Likewise, in the noble and virtuous places it is graver in sin than elsewhere.

As for its variation according to the doer: fornication by a free person is more heinous than by a slave. For this reason his penalty is half of the penalty for the free.

Fornication by a married person is more heinous than by an unmarried one, and by an elderly person more heinous than by a young one.

For this reason, among the three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify, and for whom there is a painful punishment, is the elderly adulterer. Fornication by a scholar is more heinous than by an ignorant person, because of his knowledge of its ugliness and its consequences, and his committing it with insight. Fornication by one able to do without it is more heinous than by a poor, incapable person.

(Section)

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 23, verses 10–11:

Al-Firdaws (paradise, the highest garden): a name said to apply to the whole of Paradise. It is also said to refer to its best and highest part, as though it has a greater claim to this name than the other gardens.

The root meaning of al-firdaws is "orchard," and al-faradis are orchards. Ka'b said: "It is the orchard in which there are grapevines."

Al-Layth said: "Al-firdaws is a garden with vines. It is said: 'a firdaws vineyard,' meaning one trained on trellises (mu'arrash)."

Al-Dahhak said: "It is the garden thick with trees," and this is the view preferred by al-Mubarrad.

He also said, regarding what I have heard of the speech of the Arabs: al-firdaws is "dense trees, most of which are grapevines, and its plural is al-faradis."

He said: "For this reason the gate called Bab al-Faradis in Syria was so named." He recited a verse by Jarir:

"I said to the riding party when the journey pressed on us: 'O how far apart are the gates of al-Faradis!'"

Mujahid said: "This orchard is in Byzantine (Rumi) language." This was also the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, who said: "It is in Byzantine, transferred into the language of the Arabs."

He said: "Its reality is that it is the orchard that gathers everything found in orchards."

Hassan said:

"Indeed the reward of God is every eternal garden, and in al-Firdaws they will abide."

(Digression)
Sometimes Allah, glorified is He, moves from mentioning an individual to mentioning the species, as in His saying: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest﴾.
Here, "the one created from an extract of clay" is Adam, and "the one placed as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest" is his offspring.

(Chapter: On the stages of the son of Adam from the time of his being a sperm-drop until his settling in Paradise or in Hell)

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did indeed create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. Then indeed you, after that, are to die. Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised up﴾.

He, glorified is He, thus encompassed the states of the son of Adam from before he was a sperm-drop, indeed from being dust and water, until the time of his being resurrected on the Day of Resurrection. The first stage of his creation is that he is "an extract of clay," then after that "a extract of despised water," which is the sperm-drop that is drawn from the whole body. It remains thus for forty days. Then Allah, glorified is He, turns that sperm-drop into a clot, which is a black piece of blood, and it remains thus for another forty days. Then He, glorified is He, transforms it into a lump (mudghah), which is a piece of flesh, for forty days. In this stage, its limbs, its form, its shape and its configuration are determined.

There is disagreement concerning which of its organs is first formed and created.
Some said it is the heart.
Others said it is the brain.
Others said it is the liver.
Others said it is the spinal column (faqar al-zahr).

The proponents of the first view argued that the heart is the organ and the foundation, the source of innate heat (al-hararah al-ghariziyyah), the composite of life; therefore it must be the first to be created. They said: the dissectors have reported that they found in the sperm, at the completion of its congealing, a black dot.

Those who said it is the brain argued that the brain is the principal organ of the human being among animals, the gathering place of the senses, and that what is specific to animals is sensation and voluntary movement, and the origin of these is the brain, from which they emanate. Since what is specific to animals is sensation and voluntary movement, and these come from this organ, it must be the first in existence and formation.

Those who said it is the liver argued that it is the organ from which growth and nourishment come, by which the animal subsists. They said: the natural order requires that the first to form be the liver, then the heart, then the brain, because the first distinguishing feature of the animal is growth, and at this time it has no need of sensation or voluntary movement, for it is considered like a plant; so at that time it needs nothing but growth.

For this reason, sensation and volition only come to it when the soul is attached to it, and that is in the fourth stage of its formation. Thus the first of the organs created in it is the instrument of growth, and that is the liver. What the dissectors have observed, to the point that they are superior in this matter, is that the first thing that becomes apparent in the formation of the animal's body is three dots close to one another, which one imagines to be the outline of the liver, the heart and the brain; then some of them grow further apart from one another over the course of the days of pregnancy. This is the extent of what is known to the dissectors.

As for these dots being earlier and prior, they have no evidence for this except reason, preference and analogy, and Allah knows best.

(Section)
Then its joints, bones, veins and nerves are determined, and the hearing, sight and mouth are split open, and its throat is opened after having been closed, so the tongue is fitted into it, and its shape and form are outlined, its bones are clothed with flesh, and its bones are bound to one another most firmly and strongly. This is the "binding" (asr) of which He said: ﴿We created them and strengthened their binding﴾.
From it comes the word "isar," the bond by which something is tied, and from it comes "asir" (prisoner).

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, Abu Hilal narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: When the Prophet of Allah Dawud (peace be upon him) mentioned the punishment of Allah, his joints would become loose, and nothing would hold them together but the binding; and when he mentioned the mercy of Allah, they would return.

(Section)
Buqrat (Hippocrates) said in the third treatise of the Book of Embryos: "I will tell you: I saw the semen come into being. A woman in the household had a precious female slave, and she did not want her to become pregnant lest her price decrease. The slave heard the women saying that when a woman wants to conceive, the man's semen does not come out of her but remains retained. She understood this and began to watch herself, and at certain times she felt that it had not come out of her. The news reached me, so I ordered her to jump backward; she jumped seven jumps, and the semen fell from her with a sound like an egg, not cooked, its outer shell having been removed, and its moisture remained inside the membrane." He said: "I also say that the superfluities of the womb flow from the mother so that the fetus may be nourished by them." He said: "What appears are the fine white nerves, which I saw in the middle of the navel, and they are nowhere except the navel, because the spirit only opens a path for the soul there." Then he said: "I also say something else, apparent, that everyone who desires knowledge knows, and I clarify it with measurements: the semen is in the membrane, and it is nourished by the blood that gathers from the woman and descends to the womb." He said: "The semen attracts air and breathes in these membranes, through the causes we mentioned, and it grows from the blood that flows down from the woman." He said: "Menstruation does not flow as long as the woman is pregnant, if her child is healthy, from the first month of her pregnancy to the ninth month. But all the blood that comes from the whole body gathers around the fetus at the upper membrane, with the attraction of the soul, and the navel is the path of its arrival to the fetus, so nourishment enters to it and nourishes it and increases its growth."

He said: "When the semen remains for a while, other membranes are created for it, which extend inward from the first membrane, and they are of various kinds and many."
"As for their nature, it is like the first membrane." He said: "Some of these membranes are created first, and some are created after the second month, and some are created in the third month, and all of them do not show their benefits when first created, but some extend over the semen so that their benefits appear first, and some do not appear until later. Therefore some of them are created in the first month, some in the second month, and some in the third. And the navel is as if some of them were tied to others in the middle of the membranes; the navel is the one through which it breathes and is nourished."
"When the blood descends and the fetus is nourished by it, the membranes come between it and the fetus." For this reason He, the Exalted, says: ﴿He creates you in the bellies of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses﴾.
Each of these membranes has a darkness specific to it. He, glorified is He, mentioned the stages of its creation and its transfer through them from state to state, and mentioned the darknesses of the membranes that are upon the fetus. Most of the commentators said: they are the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta (mashimah), since each of these is a membrane over the fetus. Others said: they are the darkness of the loins of the fathers, the darkness of the wombs of the mothers, and the darkness of the placenta. Weaker than this view is the view of those who said: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the belly, and the darkness of the womb, for night and day are equal in relation to the fetus.

Buqrat said: when a woman conceives, she does not feel pain from the gathering of the blood that descends and collects around her womb, and she does not feel weakness as she feels when menstruation descends, because her blood does not surge each month, but it descends into the womb little by little every day, a calm descent without pain. When it reaches the womb, the fetus is nourished by it and grows.
He said: "Not long after this, when flesh and body are created for the fetus, the membranes form, and as it grows, the membranes also grow, and they acquire a cavity outside the fetus. When the blood descends from the mother, the fetus draws it and is nourished by it and increases its flesh, and the bad blood, which is not fit for nourishment, descends to the channels of the membranes. Likewise, the membranes that, once they have a cavity, receive the blood, are called the placenta (mashimah)."
He said: "When the fetus is complete and its form is perfected, and it draws blood for its nourishment in the proper amount, the membranes widen and the placenta appears, which is among the organs we mentioned. If its inside widens, its outside widens too, because it is more fitting for that, since it has a place to extend to."
I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: From here it is that a pregnant woman does not menstruate; rather, what she sees of blood is diseased blood, not the regular menstrual blood. This is one of the two narrations from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and it is the well-known position of the school of Ahmad, whose adherents know no other, and it is the position of Abu Hanifah. Al-Shafi'i, in a narration from Aisha, and Imam Ahmad, in a narration from him which our Shaykh (Ibn Taymiyyah) preferred, held that what she sees of blood at the time of her customary period is menstruation.

The argument for this view is clear: it is the generality of the evidences indicating that a woman abandons fasting and prayer when she sees her customary blood at the time of menstruation, and Allah and His Messenger did not make exceptions for one state over another. As for the claim that the blood is directed to the nourishment of the child, it is known that this does not prevent some of it from remaining and coming out at the time of menstruation as surplus over the child's nourishment. So there is no contradiction between the child's nourishment and the mother's menstruation.

The proponents of the other view argue with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "A pregnant woman is not to be had sexually until she gives birth, nor a non-pregnant woman until she has been purified by one menstruation." So he made the menstrual period a sign of the absence of pregnancy. If a pregnant woman menstruated, the menstrual period would not be a sign of the clearing of her womb. The others answer this by saying that menstruation is an apparent sign, so when pregnancy appears through it, we realize it was not a proof; for this reason the waiting period is judged to end by menstruation apparently, and then the woman is shown to be pregnant. And the Prophet ﷺ divided women into two categories: a woman known to be pregnant, and a woman presumed to be pregnant; so he made the waiting period of the first end with delivery and of the second with a menstruation.

This is what the hadith indicates; it does not indicate that what a pregnant woman sees of blood at the time of her customary period is one during which she fasts and prays.

(Section)
Buqrat said: "Bones harden from heat, because heat hardens the bones and binds them to one another like a tree whose parts are bound together." He said: "The sinew was made inward and outward; the head was placed between the two shoulders, and the upper arms and forearms are on the two sides, and the space between the two legs is likewise opened. In each joint a sinew is placed which binds and tightens it." I say: this is the binding (asr) with which man is bound. He said: "The mouth opens of its own accord; the nose and the two ears are formed of flesh; the two ears were pierced, then the two eyes after that, and they were filled with clear moisture."

The Prophet ﷺ used to say in his prostration: "My face prostrates to the One who created it, shaped it, and split open its hearing and its sight." The conjunction "and" does not necessarily imply order, but the mention of hearing first in the wording suits its precedence in existence. Then the intestines expand after that and acquire a cavity; the joints become bound; the breath rises to the mouth and nose; inhalation enters through the mouth and nose; the belly and intestines open; and the breath comes out to the mouth instead of the navel. When what we have mentioned is complete, the time of the fetus's emergence arrives, and surplus from its stomach and intestines descends to the bladder, and there is a passage from the stomach and intestines to the bladder,
and from it to the urinary passage. All these open only, and their cavity widens, by inhalation, and by it some parts become separated from one another according to their shapes. He said: "When the belly widens and the cavity of the intestines becomes clear, a passage to the bladder and the urethra comes into being by necessity."

He said: "When the semen is formed, each part of it goes to its companion: bones to bones, sinews to sinews, and likewise all the organs; then the fetus is assembled." Then he said: "We have seen many women whose fetuses have been spoiled in them, and then they came out after thirty days." Then he said: "Do you not see that when a fetus falls after thirty days, you see its joints assembled?" And he said: "This is known by looking at the miscarriage, because when it falls, it does not fall by our device but by its own nature." Then he said: "When the fetus is assembled and its joints are complete, its organs are enlarged and its bones are hardened, it draws from the body a rich blood, and this is retained and moves at the ends of the bones like the movement of the tips of trees." He said: "Likewise the fetus, and it turns over."

(Section)
He said in the second treatise of this book: "Then the fetus is assembled, and the male is complete at thirty-two days, and the female at forty-two days, and it may exceed these days a little or fall short a little." He said: "The fetus is complete and takes shape, if it is a male, in thirty-two days, and if it is a female, in forty-two days." He said: "We observe this from the purification of the woman, for if she gives birth to a female, she is purified in forty-two days, which is the greatest period a woman is withheld until she is purified in forty-two days when she gives birth to a female; and it may be in an odd case that she is purified in thirty-five days. If she gives birth to a male, she is purified in thirty-two days if she is withheld much; and it may be in an odd case that she remains in twenty-five days."
He said: "Menstrual blood comes out from where the fetus comes out, and just as the male takes shape in thirty-two days, so the mother's purification after her delivery is in thirty-two days; and the woman, when she gives birth to a female, is purified in forty-two days, according to the number of days in which it is assembled." Then he said: "The postpartum woman bleeds for many days after her delivery, because when she conceived, the fetus did not need much nourishment at first, until it was complete; when it had forty-two days, it was nourished as it should be, and what gathered of blood during the forty days that descends to the fetus remained until the woman gave birth; so when she delivers, it descends for forty days."

I say: In this section there are two sound hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which we will mention, and we will mention how each confirms the other; then we will examine the words of Buqrat and clarify what is in them, by the power, success, teaching and guidance of Allah.

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us, and he is the truthful one whose word is believed (al-sadiq al-masdub)

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 23, verses 12–16 (part 2 of 3):

"Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's womb as a creation for forty days, then he becomes a clinging clot (*'alaqah*) of similar duration, then he becomes a lump of flesh (*mudghah*) of similar duration. Then Allah sends the angel, who breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term of life, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. By He other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you may act by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is no distance between him and it except a cubit, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed one of you may act by the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is no distance between him and it except a cubit, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

In another route: "Indeed the creation of the son of Adam is gathered in his mother's womb for forty."

In another: "Forty nights."

Al-Bukhari said: "Forty days and forty nights."

In some of its routes: "Then Allah sends an angel with four words, and he writes his deeds, his term, his provision, and whether he is wretched or blessed. Then He breathes the spirit into him..." and the hadith continues.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, which he traces to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The angel enters upon the drop (*nutfah*) after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights, and says: 'O Lord, is he wretched or blessed?' and both are recorded. Then he says: 'O Lord, is it male or female?' and both are recorded. He writes his deeds, his traces, his term and his provision. Then the scrolls are folded, and nothing is added to them or subtracted from them."

Imam Ahmad said: "Sufyan related to me from Amr, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The angel enters upon the drop after it has settled in the womb for forty nights, and says: O Lord, is he wretched or blessed? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, and both are recorded. Then they say: is it male or female? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, and both are recorded. Then he records his deeds, his traces, his affliction and his provision. Then the scroll is folded, and nothing is added to what is in it or subtracted from it.'"

In Sahih Muslim, from Amir ibn Wathilah, that he heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: "The wretched one is he who is wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed one is he who takes admonition from others."

He came to a man among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah called Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari and related to him that statement of Ibn Mas'ud. He said: "How can a man be wretched without deeds?" The man said to him: "Are you surprised at this? I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

'When the drop has passed forty-two nights, Allah sends to it an angel who shapes it, and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh and its bones. Then he says: O Lord, is it male or female? Your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes. Then he says: O Lord, its term? Your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes. Then he says: O Lord, its provision? Your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes. Then the angel comes out with the scroll in his hand, and he neither adds to what he was commanded nor subtracts from it.'"

In another wording: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say with these two ears of mine: 'Indeed the drop falls into the womb for forty nights, then an angel descends upon it.'" Zuhayr said: "I think he said: 'He who creates it, and says: O Lord, is it male or female? So Allah makes it male or female. Then he says: O Lord, is it complete or incomplete? So Allah makes it complete or incomplete. Then he says: O Lord, what is its provision, what is its term, and what is its creation? Then Allah makes it wretched or blessed.'"

In another wording: "Indeed, there is an angel appointed over the womb, and when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills to create something by the permission of Allah, [it is] for about forty nights..." and he mentioned the hadith.

The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud and the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd agree on the occurrence of a matter and a state of the drop after the forty. The hadith of Hudhayfah is explicit in its explanation that this writing takes place after the forty and before the breathing of the spirit, as previously mentioned in the narration of al-Bukhari.

As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, one of its wordings agrees with the hadith of Hudhayfah, even though that determination and writing after the forty and before the breathing of the spirit is in it, as previously mentioned in the narration of al-Bukhari, whose wording is:

"Then Allah sends to it an angel with four words, and he writes his deeds, his provision, his term, and whether he is wretched or blessed. Then He breathes the spirit into him."

This is explicit that the writing and the angel's questioning take place before the breathing of the spirit into him, and it agrees with the hadith of Hudhayfah on that point.

As for his other wording: "Then He breathes the spirit into him and he is commanded with four words," it is not explicit, because the words he is commanded with would then be after the breathing of the spirit. This clause is conjoined with the conjunction "and" (*wa*), and it may be conjoined to the clause that follows it. It may also be conjoined to the preceding clause of the speech, meaning: He gathers his creation in these stages, and the angel is commanded to write his provision, his term, and his deeds. The statement "Then He breathes the spirit into him" comes between the clauses as an explanation of the delay of the breathing of the spirit after the stages of the drop, the clot and the lump.

Consider how He used "then" (*thumma*) in the clause about breathing the spirit, and "and" (*wa*) in His saying "and he is commanded with four words." Thus all the hadiths agree, praise be to Allah.

What remains is to ask: the hadith of Hudhayfah indicates that the beginning of the formation is after the first forty, while the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud indicates that it is after the third forty. How can they be reconciled?

It is said: as for the hadith of Hudhayfah, it is explicit that this takes place after the forty. As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, it contains no reference to the time of shaping and formation; it only explains the stages of the drop and its transformations after every forty, and that after the third forty the spirit is breathed into it. The hadith of Hudhayfah does not address this, but it is specific to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. So the two hadiths share the occurrence of a matter after the first forty. The hadith of Hudhayfah is specific in that the beginning of its shaping and creation is after the first forty, and the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is specific in that the breathing of the spirit into it is after the third forty. The two hadiths share the angel's seeking permission from his Lord, Glorified is He, to determine the state of the child during that period. Thus the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agree, and some of them confirm others.

The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud contains two matters: the matter of the drop and its transformations, and the matter of the angel's writing what Allah decrees concerning it. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed of both matters in the hadith. Imam Ahmad said: "Hushaym related to us: Ali ibn Zayd informed us: I heard Abu Utbah ibn Abdullah narrate: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

'Indeed the drop remains in the womb for forty days in its condition, not changing. When forty have passed for it, it becomes a clot, then a lump of flesh in the same manner, then bones in the same manner. When He wills to fashion its creation, Allah sends to it the angel, who says, the angel charged with it: O Lord, male or female? Wretched or blessed? Short or tall? Deficient or complete? Its sustenance and its term? Healthy or sick? He says: and he writes all of that.'"

This hadith contains the cure, and what occurs after the third forty is the fashioning of the creation at the time of the breathing of the spirit into it.

There is no doubt that at the breathing of the spirit into it and its attachment to it, there occurs in its creation matters additional to the formation that was after the first forty. The first was the beginning of the formation, and this is its perfecting and the completion of what was decreed for it, just as Allah, Glorified is He, created the earth before the heaven, then created the heaven, then after that arranged the earth, spread it out and completed its creation. That is His action in the dwelling-place, and this is His action in the one who dwells in it. Moreover, the formation and shaping arise in the drop after the forty gradually, bit by bit, as plants grow. This is observed in animals and plants, as when you consider the state of the chick in the egg. The confusion arises only from failing to understand the words of Allah the Exalted and His Messenger (ﷺ). The confusion is in our understanding, not in the explanation of the infallible one.

And Allah is the One whose help is sought. This has sufficed you, praise be to Allah, from the labored efforts of the commentators, so ponder it, weigh it against this combined view, and with Allah is success.

(Section)

Hippocrates said in his book *al-Ghidha* (On Nutrition): The shaping of the fetus occurs in thirty-five days, its first movement in seventy days, and its completion in one hundred and ten days. Other fetuses are shaped in fifty days, and they move with the first movement at one hundred days, and they complete at three hundred. Other fetuses are shaped in forty days, they move at eighty days, and they are born at two hundred and forty days. Other fetuses are shaped in forty-five days, they move at ninety days, and they are born at two hundred and seventy days. He said: As for birth, it occurs in the seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth months.

I say: Movement is of two kinds. One is natural, involuntary movement, and this occurs before the attachment of the spirit to it. As for voluntary movement, it does not occur except after the breathing of the spirit. For this reason Hippocrates distinguished between the first and the second movement.

I say: What the true revelation has indicated about the Creator of mankind is that creation passes through a new stage every forty days. It is first a drop for forty days, then a clot for the same, then a lump for the same, then the spirit is breathed into it after one hundred and twenty days.

This is as though you were witnessing it directly. Whatever contradicts it has no direct observation behind it. The most that he has is a flawed analogy and an anatomical examination that does not encompass knowledge of the origin of what he observed, or the imitation of a single non-infallible person. Everything that came from him was followed by others who accepted it. The one who believes in it thinks it is a matter agreed upon among the naturalists, while its root is one error, which the first man made and then others imitated after him. Those people did not witness what they reported about it.

The most they have is that they dissected pregnant women, living and dead, and found the fetus in the womb in the form they described. But they have no knowledge of what lies beyond that, such as the beginning of pregnancy and the changes in the state of the drop. Suppose their imitator were to press the point:

We may assume that they observed a virgin from the time she was penetrated, then counted her days until she reached what they mentioned, then dissected her and found the matter in the form they described. This is the utmost lie and slander, for those people did not claim this, and how could they claim it when they report that after so many days the state of the pregnancy will become such and such? What they have is universals and analogies: it should be such and such, and the natural order requires such and such.

Many of them derive it from the movements of the moon, its waxing and waning, and from the movements of the sun, and from the trine, the quadrature, the sextile and the opposition. Others among them refuted them and nullified this against them in many respects. Some referred it to what is more proper, more suitable and more fitting. Others referred it to the days of the seas and the change of their nature. Some of these refuted others and nullified their statements with what we have omitted for fear of prolixity.

The soundest of what they have is dissection and complete induction, which admit no exception. We do not deny that, but there is nothing in it that contradicts revelation concerning the differences among fetuses at all. Among the things that show that these people did not report this from direct observation is their saying that the fetus born in the seventh month becomes a *daydiyyan* (the stage of the seminal drop) in nine days, then *damawiyyan* (the stage of blood) in eight other days, then *lahmiyyan* (the stage of flesh) in nine other days, and receives the form in twelve other days. When these days are added together they make thirty-five days, so they made it a lump of flesh within the first forty.

This is clearly and certainly a lie. The fetus becomes flesh only after the eightieth day. Such a matter cannot be known except by revelation or direct observation, and both are absent from them. What they have is an analogy by which they inferred the states of fetuses from the months of their birth. They then judged that every fetus born in a month of the birth months should be a *daydiyyan*, that is, a drop of such and such a number of days, a *damawiyyan*, that is, a clot of such and such a number of days, and a *lahmiyyan*, that is, a lump of such and such a number of days. Then they halved that number and made it the time of the fetus's movement.

They lied about the All-Knowing Creator in His creation, as they lied about Him in His attributes and names. Those people had no share of the knowledge that the messengers brought. Rather, they were, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾. What does the one who rejects and turns away from what the messengers brought attain? The most he attains is knowledge of natural matters, in which there is truth and falsehood, and mathematical matters that involve much labor and little benefit, and astronomical matters whose falsehood is many times their truth. How far is the knowledge received from the descending revelation from the opinion derived from a fleeting view? How far is the knowledge taken from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from Jibril, from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from the opinion taken from the view of a man whose heart has not been illumined by the light of revelation for a moment of an eye? He has only his intuition and his guessing. The attachment of what all rational people perceive by their intellects to what the messengers brought is like the relation of a weak lamp to the light of the sun.

You will not find, even if you lived the lifespan of Noah, a single question on which all rational people agree against what the messengers brought in any matter whatsoever. The prophets did not bring anything that contradicts clear reason at all. Rather, they brought what reason cannot perceive. What the messengers brought, alongside reason, falls into three categories with no fourth: a category which reason and natural disposition attest to; a category which reason attests to in general but does not guide to its details; and a category for which reason has no capacity to perceive. As for the fourth category, that which clear reason deems impossible and attests to its falsehood, the messengers are free of it. Yet many ignorant people who claim knowledge and insight think that some of what the messengers brought belongs to this category. This is either because of their ignorance of what the messengers brought, or their ignorance of the judgment of reason, or both.

(Section)

On the states of the fetus after its movement and its transformation at the completion of half a year. At this time it happens to the fetus that its membrane and the veils around it are torn, and that it moves from its place toward the mouth of the womb. If the fetus is strong and its membranes and its umbilical cord are weaker, the birth is complete. If the fetus is weak while its membranes and umbilical cord are stronger, then either they are torn in part and it is not born, so it remains sick for forty days until the end of the eighth month completes...

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 23, verse 12–16 (part 3 of 3):

If the child is born during these forty days, it dies, and neither its upbringing nor its survival is possible. If its membranes are torn completely, so that it cannot be saved from this, and it is not born, it dies; and if it does not miscarry, the pregnant woman is killed. If its membranes are torn in a way that can be remedied, it remains and does not die, and it stays in its place toward which it moved and turned, at the mouth of the womb. Illness afflicts them during these forty days if they are not born after they have moved, because they turn over from the place in which they grew and their positions change, and the navel is dislodged by its movement. Also, their mothers may fall ill at that time because of the stretching of the membranes and the dislodging of the navel that is connected to the womb in them. Also, when the fetus's bond is loosened, it becomes heavy upon its mother.

(Section)

When the fetus has been formed and the Creator, the Fashioner, has shaped it, it is created with its head upward and its legs downward. When God permits its emergence, it turns over and its head comes to be downward, so its head precedes the rest of its body. This is agreed upon by physicians and anatomists, and this is part of the perfection of divine care for the fetus and its mother, because when its head comes out first, the emergence of the rest of its body is easier, without any part of them needing to bend. For if the fetus's legs came out first, it could not be assured that it would become caught in the womb at its hands; and if one of its legs came out, it could not be assured that it would become hooked and caught in the womb as it develops. If both hands came out, it could not be assured that it would become caught at its head, either because it twists backward, or because the navel twists around its neck or shoulder, since when the fetus descends and reaches a place where the navel is stretched, it twists there around its neck and shoulder. Thus, from that, one of two things results: either the navel pulls at it, so the mother suffers extreme pain, and then the fetus either dies or its emergence is difficult, and it comes out sick and swollen. So the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges required that it turn over in the belly, so that its head comes out first and the rest of the body follows the head.

(Section)

Concerning the reason why a child born at eight months does not survive, while one born at seven, nine, or ten months does survive.

When the fetus completes seven months, it develops a strong movement, which it makes naturally for turning and emerging. If the fetus is strong among those children who have by nature great strength in their constitution and make-up, so that by its movement it is able to tear the membranes surrounding it that are connected to the womb, until it passes through and emerges from them, it comes out in the seventh month strong, healthy and sound, the movement not having harmed it and the turning not having made it ill. But if it is too weak for that, then either it perishes because of the harm and pain it suffers from the movement of turning, and comes out dead, or it remains in the belly and becomes ill, and remains in its illness for about forty days until it recovers, revives and grows strong. When it is born within the eighth month, it is born while still ill, not having been freed from its pain, so it perishes and does not survive and is not raised. But if it remains in the womb until it passes these forty days into the ninth month, and grows strong, revives, and its time of illness is far behind it, it is likely to survive; and those most deserving of survival are those who remained longest in the womb after the turning, namely those born in the tenth month. As for those born between the tenth and ninth months, their condition in this respect is according to nearness and distance.

Another scholar said: the reason that a child born at eight months cannot survive is that two kinds of harm follow upon it: one is its turning in the seventh month within the womb for birth, and the second is the change of condition between its place in the womb and its place in the air. Although this change may happen to all fetuses, the child born at seven months escapes from the womb before the harm within it reaches him, following the turning and the illnesses that occur inside the womb. The child born at seven months and at ten months remains in the womb until it recovers and is saved from those illnesses, so the two harms do not follow upon it together. The child born at eight months has the two harms following upon it together, and therefore it cannot survive, since all fetuses in the eighth month are afflicted with illness.

What indicates this is that you find all pregnant women in the eighth month in a worse condition and heavier than in the months before this month and after it, and the conditions of mothers are connected to the conditions of the fetuses.

(Section)

The crying of a child at the hour of its birth indicates its health, strength and vigor. When the child places its hand, thumb or finger on a limb of its body, this is a sign of pain in that limb. Every animal by nature indicates what pains it in its body, either with its paw, its mouth, its head or its tail. So when the child lacks speech, it points with its finger or hand to the place of its pain, like a dumb animal.

(Section)

Concerning how children, while in the womb, are stronger than they are after their birth, more patient and more able to bear what befalls them. Likewise, the care for them after their birth is more emphatic and the caution for them is greater. For the branches of a tree and its boughs, as long as they are adhering to the tree and connected to it, are hardly shaken or uprooted by violent winds; but when they are separated from it and planted in other places, they are struck by calamity and reached by the slightest wind that blows, until it uproots them. Likewise, the fetus, as long as it is in the womb, grows strong and patient against what befalls it and what it suffers from poor management and harm, more than it can bear even the slightest of these after its birth and separation from the womb. Likewise, the fruit on the tree is stronger and more firm than after it is cut from it.

Since separation from everything customary and familiar, by moving away from it, is very difficult for the one who undertakes it, especially when the move is all at once, the fetus, upon separation from the womb, moves at once from what it has become accustomed to and familiar with in all its conditions, and the severity of this move upon it is greater than the severity of a move by gradual stages.

For this reason Hippocrates said: "It may be known with the least effort and ease that bad regimen of food and drink, if it continues in one unchanging manner, resembling itself always, is more reliable, safer and further from danger in seeking health for bodies than if a man changes his regimen all at once to a better food." The fetus moves from what it has become accustomed to in its nourishment, breathing, entrances and what surrounds it, in a single instant.

This is the first hardship it meets in the world, after which hardships gather around it until the last of them is the supreme hardship beyond which there is no hardship, or the supreme ease beyond which there is no weariness. For this reason it does not cry at the arrival of this hardship upon it, along with what it meets of the Satan's prodding and his jab in its side.

(Section)

The fetus in the womb was nourished by what suited it, and by nature it drew from its mother's blood the amount suited to it. After its emergence it likewise draws from milk what suits it, but it draws by its appetite and will, so it exceeds the amount it needs, while the milk may be bad and diseased just as it may be sound. Likewise it suffers vomiting and nausea, and it draws in the humors of its body, and it is afflicted with pains, aches and calamities that did not befall it in the belly. In the belly it had membranes and veils that prevented harm from reaching it; but when it was born, it was provided with other membranes and veils to which it was not accustomed or habituated, and it is sometimes exposed to heat, cold and wind. It draws from its navel, which is the most delicate, most temperate and healthiest thing, the very thing that keeps the mother's heart and pulsing veins sound. So it resembles one who enters a bath and draws in the delicate, temperate air, and then comes out of it all at once, naked, into the harsh and harmful wind.

In sum, it has moved away from what it was used to and accustomed to, all at once, to something more severe and difficult for it. This is part of the perfect wisdom of the All-Creating, the All-Knowing, to train His servant to leave his habits and familiar things for what is better, more beneficial and more suitable for him. God, exalted is He, pointed to this in His saying: ﴿You shall surely ride from stage to stage﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 84:19], meaning state after state. Its first stages are that it is a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then a fetus, then a newborn, then a suckling, then weaned, then healthy or sick, rich or poor, safe or afflicted, through all the various conditions of man upon him, until he dies, then is resurrected, then is made to stand before God, Exalted, then he goes to Paradise or to the Fire. So the meaning is: you shall ride from state to state, from station to station, and from matter to matter.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "You shall surely be in the Hereafter after the first life, and you shall surely become rich after poverty and poor after wealth."

'Ata' said: "Hardship after hardship." And "tabaq" and "tabaqah" mean the state. For this reason it is said: "So-and-so was in various tabaqat," i.e., various states.

'Amr ibn al-'As said: "I was in three tabaqat," meaning three states.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: "The tabaq is the state, in its variations."

We have mentioned some of the stages of the fetus in the belly from the time it was a drop until the time of its birth. Now we mention its stages after its birth until their end, so we say:

The fetus in the womb is like the fruit on the tree in its strong connection to its place. When it reaches its completion, nothing remains but its separation, because of its weight and maturity, and the severing of the veins that hold it. Likewise, the fetus: those membranes are torn away, and the veins that hold it between the placenta and the womb are severed, and those slippery fluids become the means of easing its exit through their slipperiness; its weight and the tearing of the veins aid its emergence. The womb opens very widely, and some great joints must separate, then they rejoin in the quickest time. Skilled physicians and anatomists have acknowledged this, and they said that this is not accomplished except by divine care and a design that defeats the minds of people in grasping how it is done: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:14].

When the fetus is separated, it cries at the moment of its separation, for a natural reason, which is its parting from what it was familiar with and its place in which it was, and for an external cause, which is the Satan's jab in its side. When it is separated and its separation is complete, it stretches its hand to its mouth. When forty days have passed for it, you find it having another matter similar to what was renewed for it while in the womb, and it laughs at forty days, and that is the first time it perceives itself. When it has two months, it sees dreams. Then discernment and intellect develop with it gradually, little by little, until the age of discernment. There is no fixed age for this; among people there is one who discerns at five, as Mahmud ibn al-Rabi' said: "I remember from the Prophet ﷺ a mouthful he spat into my face from a bucket in their well, and I was the son of five years."

For this reason the age of five has been set as the limit of the child's keen hearing.

Some discern at less than that, and remember things that happened to them while under five years old.

It has been mentioned of Iyas ibn Mu'awiya that he said: "Remember the day my mother bore me, for I came out from darkness into light, then I went into darkness again." His mother was asked about that, and she said: "He spoke truly. When he was separated from me, I did not have anything to make him familiar with it, so I placed a bowl over him."

This is among the most wondrous and rare of things. When he reaches seven years, he enters the age of discernment and is commanded to pray,

as in the Musnad and the Sunan, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:

"Command your children to pray at seven years old, and strike them for it at ten years old, and separate them in their beds."

(Digression)
Sometimes Allah, glorified is He, moves from mentioning an individual to mentioning the species, as in His saying: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest﴾.
Here, "the one created from an extract of clay" is Adam, and "the one placed as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest" is his offspring.

(Chapter: On the stages of the son of Adam from the time of his being a sperm-drop until his settling in Paradise or in Hell)

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did indeed create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm place of rest. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. Then indeed you, after that, are to die. Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised up﴾.

He, glorified is He, thus encompassed the states of the son of Adam from before he was a sperm-drop, indeed from being dust and water, until the time of his being resurrected on the Day of Resurrection. The first stage of his creation is that he is "an extract of clay," then after that "a extract of despised water," which is the sperm-drop that is drawn from the whole body. It remains thus for forty days. Then Allah, glorified is He, turns that sperm-drop into a clot, which is a black piece of blood, and it remains thus for another forty days. Then He, glorified is He, transforms it into a lump (mudghah), which is a piece of flesh, for forty days. In this stage, its limbs, its form, its shape and its configuration are determined.

There is disagreement concerning which of its organs is first formed and created.
Some said it is the heart.
Others said it is the brain.
Others said it is the liver.
Others said it is the spinal column (faqar al-zahr).

The proponents of the first view argued that the heart is the organ and the foundation, the source of innate heat (al-hararah al-ghariziyyah), the composite of life; therefore it must be the first to be created. They said: the dissectors have reported that they found in the sperm, at the completion of its congealing, a black dot.

Those who said it is the brain argued that the brain is the principal organ of the human being among animals, the gathering place of the senses, and that what is specific to animals is sensation and voluntary movement, and the origin of these is the brain, from which they emanate. Since what is specific to animals is sensation and voluntary movement, and these come from this organ, it must be the first in existence and formation.

Those who said it is the liver argued that it is the organ from which growth and nourishment come, by which the animal subsists. They said: the natural order requires that the first to form be the liver, then the heart, then the brain, because the first distinguishing feature of the animal is growth, and at this time it has no need of sensation or voluntary movement, for it is considered like a plant; so at that time it needs nothing but growth.

For this reason, sensation and volition only come to it when the soul is attached to it, and that is in the fourth stage of its formation.
