Consider his first saying ﴿My Lord﴾, as he cries out to his Lord. Then he turns to the angels who were commanded to bring him before his Lord, blessed and exalted, and says (﴿Send me back﴾).

Then he mentions the reason for his request for a return: that he would take up righteous action regarding what he left behind of his wealth, his standing, his authority, his strength and his means. It is said to him (﴿No!﴾). There is no way for you to return, for you have had a life in which whoever would take heed could take heed.

Since it is the way of the Generous and Merciful to respond to one who cries out, and to grant him a respite so that he may take heed of what he missed, Allah, glorified is He, informed us that this transgressor's request for a return is a word that he utters, with no reality beneath it. His disposition and nature would refuse to perform righteous deeds even if he were answered. It is merely something he says with his tongue. And if he were sent back, he would return to what he was forbidden. And he is among the liars. Thus His judgment, the Most Judicious of judges, and His might, knowledge and praise refuse to answer him with what he asked, for there is no benefit in that.

And if he were returned, his second state would be like his first state, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, "Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." Nay, but there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾

[Section: The Divisions of the Abodes]

The third matter: Allah, glorified is He, made the abodes three: the abode of the world (dunya), the abode of the barzakh (intermediate realm), and the abode of permanence (qarar). He assigned to each abode rulings specific to it. He constituted this human being of a body and a soul (nafs). He made the rulings of the abode of the world apply to bodies and spirits in a subordinate manner. For this reason He made His legal rulings dependent upon what appears of the movements of the tongue and the limbs, even if souls conceal the opposite. And He made the rulings of the barzakh apply to spirits and bodies in a subordinate manner. Just as spirits followed bodies in the rulings of the world, suffering with their pain and rejoicing with their comfort, and it was they that engaged the causes of bliss and punishment, so bodies follow spirits in their bliss and punishment. In that state, it is the spirits that directly undergo punishment and bliss. Thus bodies here are apparent, and spirits are hidden.

The bodies are, in relation to the spirits, like graves. There, the spirits are apparent and the bodies are hidden in their graves. The rulings of the barzakh apply to the spirits, so that bliss or punishment reaches their bodies, just as the rulings of the world apply to the bodies, so that bliss or punishment reaches their spirits. So grasp this matter with full knowledge and understand it as it should be understood, and it will remove from you every doubt that may be raised against you from within or without.

Allah, glorified is He, has shown us, by His kindness, mercy and guidance, a model of this in the world: the state of the sleeper. What he is blessed with or punished with in his sleep applies to his spirit primarily, and the body follows it. It may grow strong enough to affect the body visibly. A sleeper sees that he has been struck, and he wakes to find the mark of the blow on his body. He sees that he has eaten or drunk, and he awakens to find the trace of food and drink in his mouth, and hunger and thirst have left him.

And more wondrous than that: you see the sleeper rise in his sleep, strike, lash out and defend himself as if he were awake, while he is asleep and has no awareness of any of that. This is because the ruling applied to the spirit, so it sought help from the body from outside it. Had the spirit entered it, he would have awoken and perceived. If the spirit feels pain and bliss, and that reaches its body by way of subordination, then it is likewise in the barzakh, indeed even greater, for the spirit's detachment there is more complete and stronger, while it remains attached to its body, not cut off from it entirely. When the Day of the gathering of bodies comes, and people rise from their graves, the rule, the bliss and the punishment in the spirits and bodies become manifest and fully apparent.

When you give this matter its due, it becomes clear to you that what the Messenger reported about the punishment of the grave, its bliss, its constriction and its expansiveness, its squeezing, and that it is either a pit of the Fire or a garden of the gardens of Paradise, is consistent with reason, and that it is true beyond any doubt. And whoever finds this difficult to comprehend does so from poor understanding and little knowledge, as it has been said:

"How many a critic has faulted a sound statement, and its flaw came from a sick understanding."

And more wondrous than that: you find the sleeper in one bed, while his spirit is in bliss, and he awakes with the trace of that bliss on his body; and his spirit is in punishment, and he awakes with the trace of that punishment on his body; and neither of them has any knowledge of what the other is experiencing. So the matter of the barzakh is more wondrous than that.

The fourth matter: Allah, glorified is He, made the matter of the Hereafter, and what is connected with it, unseen, and veiled it from the perception of the accountable in this abode. That is from the perfection of His wisdom, and so that believers in the unseen may be distinguished from others. The first of that is that the angels descend upon the dying person, sit near him, he sees them with his own eyes, and they converse in his presence, and with them are the shrouds and the embalming spices, either from Paradise or from the Fire. They say "Amen" to the supplications of those present, for good or for evil. Sometimes they greet the dying person, and he responds at times with a word, at times with a gesture, and at times with his heart, when he is unable to speak or gesture. Some of the dying have been heard saying: "Welcome and well come and greetings to these faces."

My teacher informed me about one of the dying, and I do not know whether he witnessed it or was told about it, that he was heard saying: "Peace upon you here," so sit; and "Peace upon you here," so sit.

The story of the weaver, may Allah have mercy on him, is well known: at death he said: "Be patient, may Allah grant you well-being, for what you have been commanded does not escape, and what you have been commanded does pass." Then he asked for water, performed ablution, prayed, then said: "Proceed to what you have been commanded," and he died.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya reported that when 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz was on the day he died, he said: "Sit me up." So they sat him up, and he said: "I am the one you commanded, and I fell short; you forbade me, and I disobeyed," three times, "but there is no god but Allah." Then he raised his head and gazed intently. They said: "You are looking with an intense gaze, Commander of the Believers." He said: "I see a presence that is neither human nor jinn." Then he passed away.

Maslama ibn 'Abd al-Malik said: When 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz was dying, we were with him in a tent. He gestured to us to leave, so we left and sat around the tent. A young servant remained with him, and we heard him recite this verse: ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter; We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth or corruption, and the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Qasas 28:83]. Then he said: "You are neither human nor jinn." Then the servant came out and gestured to us to enter, and we entered, and he had died.

Fadala ibn Dinar said: I attended Muhammad ibn Wasi' when he had been covered for death, and he began saying: "Welcome, angels of my Lord, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah." And I smelled a fragrance I had never smelled that was more fragrant. Then he fixed his gaze and died.

The reports on this are more numerous than can be counted.

More conclusive and sufficient than all of that is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿So why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you are at that moment looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾.

That is, nearer to him by Our angels and messengers, but you do not see. This is the beginning of the matter, and it is not visible to us nor observed, and it is in this abode.

Then the angel extends his hand to the spirit, takes it, and addresses it, while those present neither see nor hear him. Then it departs, and a light goes out with it like the rays of the sun, and a fragrance more pleasant than musk, while those present neither see that nor smell it. Then it ascends between two rows of angels, while those present do not see them. Then the spirit comes and witnesses the washing of the body, its shrouding and its carrying, and it says: "Hasten me, hasten me," or "Where are you taking me?", and people do not hear that. When it is placed in its niche and the earth is leveled over it, the earth does not screen the angels from reaching it. Even if a stone were hollowed out, the body placed in it and sealed with lead, that would not prevent the angels from reaching it, for these dense bodies do not prevent the spirits from passing through them. Indeed jinn are not prevented by that either. Allah, glorified is He, has made stone and earth for the angels like air for birds. The expansion and widening of the grave is for the spirit primarily, and the body follows. So the body is in a niche narrower than an arm's length, yet it is widened for it as far as its gaze reaches, following its spirit.

As for the squeezing of the grave, so that some parts of the dead are displaced, neither sense nor reason nor natural disposition rejects it. And if someone were to exhume a corpse and find its ribs as they were, undisplaced, that would not preclude that they had returned to their state after the squeezing. Thus, with the heretics and the atheists, there is nothing but mere denial of the Messenger.

Some truthful people reported that he dug three graves. When he finished them, he lay down to rest, and in a dream he saw two angels descend and stop at one of the graves. One of them said to his companion: "Write a farsakh by a farsakh" (a measure of distance). Then he stopped at the second and said: "Write a mil by a mil." Then he stopped at the third and said: "Write a fitr by a fitr." Then he awoke, and a stranger, unremarkable to anyone, was brought and buried in the first grave. Then another man was brought and buried in the second. Then a woman of distinguished standing from the notables of the town was brought, with many people around her, and she was buried in the narrow grave, the one he had heard described as "a fitr by a fitr," and the fitr is the span between the thumb and the index finger.

[Section: The Punishment of the Grave and the Punishment of the Barzakh]

The ninth matter: it should be known that the punishment of the grave and its bliss is a name for the punishment of the barzakh and its bliss, which is what lies between this world and the Hereafter. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected﴾.

This barzakh gives its inhabitants a view over both the world and the Hereafter. The punishment of the grave and its bliss were called "a garden or a pit of Fire" according to the state of most of creation. The crucified, the burned, the drowned, and the one eaten by beasts and birds have a share of the barzakh's punishment and bliss that their deeds require, even though the kinds of bliss and punishment and their modes vary. Some of the early people thought that if his body were burned with fire and became ashes, and some of it were scattered in the sea and some on land on a very windy day, he would escape that. So he instructed his sons to do that to him. Allah commanded the sea to gather what was in it, and commanded the land to gather what was in it, and then said: "Stand up," and behold, he was standing before Allah. He asked him: "What led you to do what you did?" He said: "Fear of You, O Lord, and You know best." So Allah had mercy on him. The punishment of the barzakh and its bliss were not forfeited for these parts that had come to this state. Indeed, even if the dead person were crucified on the tops of trees in the path of the winds, his body would receive its portion of the punishment of the barzakh. And if a righteous man were buried in a furnace of fire, his body would receive its portion of the bliss of the barzakh, and his spirit its portion and share. Thus Allah makes the fire, for him, coolness and safety, and the air, for others, fire or scorching wind. The elements of the world and its sources are submissive to their Lord, their Creator and their Originator. He directs them as He wills, and nothing He wills is beyond Him. Rather they are subject to His will, made subservient and submissive to His power. Whoever denies this has denied the Lord of the worlds, disbelieved in Him, and rejected His lordship.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 23, verses 115–116 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ That is, for no reason: you would not be commanded or forbidden, nor rewarded or punished. Purposelessness (ʿabath) is ugly, which shows that the ugliness of this is firmly established in natural disposition (fitar) and intellects (ʿuqul). For this reason He rejected it from them with the rejection of one who alerts them to return to their intellects and natural dispositions, and that if they reflected and observed, they would know that it is not befitting of Him, nor is it good of Him, to create His creation in vain, neither for a command nor a prohibition, nor for reward nor punishment. This shows that the goodness of command, prohibition and recompense is firmly established in the intellects and natural dispositions, and that whoever permits for Allah the neglect of this has attributed to Him what is not befitting of Him, and what His most beautiful names and highest attributes repudiate.

(Section)

Know that, were it not for obligation (taklif), the creation of man would be purposeless and aimless (sudan), and Allah is exalted above that, and He has declared Himself free of it just as He declared Himself free of defects and deficiencies. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ And He said: ﴿Does man think he will be left aimless?﴾

Al-Shafiʿi said: "He is not commanded and not forbidden." It is known that leaving man like the beasts, neglected and idle, contradicts wisdom, for he was created for the sake of his perfection, and his perfection is to be one who knows his Lord, loves Him, and stands in His worship. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me.﴾

And He said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is capable of all things and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾

And He said: ﴿That you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

This knowledge and this worship are the ultimate purpose of creation and command, and they are the greatest perfection of man. Allah, the Exalted, out of His care for him and His mercy toward him, presented him with this perfection, prepared for him its apparent and hidden means, and empowered him to attain them.

The basis of obligation rests upon Islam, faith (iman) and excellence (ihsan), and all of these return to thanking the Benefactor, in all its subtle and great aspects, from Him: exalting Him, revering Him, and dealing with Him in the manner befitting Him. So His favours are remembered and thanked, so that He is not disbelieved in, obeyed so that He is not disobeyed, and remembered so that He is not forgotten. This is together with the fact that obligation includes the characterising of the servant with every beautiful trait, his establishing of every beautiful deed and upright speech, and his avoidance of every evil trait, abandoning of every ugly deed and false speech. Thus, obligation includes noble character, excellent deeds, truthful speech, kindness to creation, the perfecting of the self with various perfections, and the shunning and purification of its opposites. Along with this, it exposes him, through that obligation, to abundant and lasting reward and to dwelling near his Lord in the abode of permanence. So which of the two matters is more befitting to wisdom: this, or sending him aimlessly like horses, mules and donkeys, eating, drinking and mating like beasts? Would His sacred perfection require that? Exalted is Allah, the True King, there is no god but He, Lord of the Noble Throne. And how could such perfection accommodate folding up the carpet of command and prohibition, reward and punishment, abandoning the sending of messengers, the sending down of books, the legislating of laws, and the establishing of rulings? Has anyone who attributed to Him the opposite of this known Allah? Is this not only from evil opinion of Him? He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They did not esteem Allah with the esteem due to Him, when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being."﴾

Thus the goodness of obligation in the intellects is like the goodness of benevolence, bestowal, favour and bounty; indeed it is among the most eloquent forms of benevolence and bestowal. For this reason He named that a blessing, a favour, a grace and a mercy, and informed that rejoicing in it is better than rejoicing in the blessings shared between the righteous and the wicked. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief?﴾

Here, the blessing of Allah is His blessing in Muhammad ﷺ and what He sent him with of guidance and the religion of truth.

And He said: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were in clear error.﴾

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were in clear error, and [He has sent him to] others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

And He said: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ And He said: ﴿Say: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾

And He said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion.﴾

And He said: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you and what He sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, by which He instructs you.﴾

And He said: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in distress; but Allah has endeared to you faith and made it attractive in your hearts, and made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the rightly guided, as a bounty and favour from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ And He said to His Messenger: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and taught you what you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been great.﴾ And is there, in truth, any blessing and favour other than that and its consequences and fruit in hearts and bodies, in this world and the Hereafter? And is there anything in sound intellects and upright natural disposition better than that, and more befitting to the perfection of the Lord and His names and attributes?

(Section)

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember? To Him is your return, all of you, the promise of Allah, true. He originates creation, then repeats it, that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

Now reflect on how the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them comprised truth at the beginning, the middle and the end; that they were created with truth, for truth, and bearing witness to truth. And He, the Exalted, rejected the one who supposed otherwise, saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾

Then He declared Himself free of this supposition, which contradicts His wisdom, knowledge and praise, saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the True King.﴾

Reflect on what is in these two names, "the True King," of refutation of this supposition which His enemies imagined, since it contradicts the perfection of His kingship and His being the Truth; for the True King is the one to whom command and prohibition belong, so He disposes of His creation by His word and command. This is the difference between "king" (malik) and "owner" (malik/mālik): the owner disposes by his action, and the king disposes by his action and command. The Lord, the Exalted, is the Owner of the kingdom, so He disposes by His action and command.

Whoever thinks that He created His creation in vain, not commanding them nor forbidding them, has impugned His kingship and has not esteemed Him with the esteem due to Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They did not esteem Allah with the esteem due to Him, when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being."﴾ Whoever denies the law of Allah, His command and His prohibition, and makes creation like grazing livestock, has impugned the kingship of Allah and has not esteemed Him with the esteem due to Him.

Likewise, His being the God of creation requires the perfection of His essence, attributes and names, and the occurrence of His acts in the most perfect and complete manner. Just as His essence is true, His speech is true, His promise is true, His command is true, and all His acts are true, and His recompense, which entails His law and religion, and the Last Day, is true; so whoever denies any of that has not described Allah as the Absolute Truth from every aspect and in every respect. For His being true entails His law, religion, reward and punishment. How, then, could one suppose of the True King that He would create His creation in vain, and leave them aimless, not commanding them, not forbidding them, not rewarding them, not punishing them? As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Does man think he will be left aimless?﴾

Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Neglected, not commanded and not forbidden."

Others said: "He is not recompensed for good and evil, nor rewarded, nor punished." The two statements are mutually implicative: al-Shafiʿi mentioned the cause of recompense, reward and punishment, which is command and prohibition, and the other mentioned the consequence of command and prohibition, which is the cause of recompense, reward and punishment.

Then reflect on His saying after that: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned.﴾ Whoever did not leave him, while a drop, aimless, but rather transformed the drop and turned it until it became more complete than it was, which is the clot; then transformed the clot until it became more complete than it was, until He created it and perfected its form, arranging it by His direction and wisdom through the stages of its perfections, until its perfection ended in a sound human being. How then would He leave him aimless, not driving him to the ultimate perfection for which he was created?

When the wise, discerning person contemplates the conditions of the drop from its origin to its end, it guides him to the Resurrection and the prophethoods, just as it guides him to the existence and oneness of the Creator and the attributes of His perfection. Just as the conditions of the drop from its beginning to its end show the perfection of the power of the Originator and Fashioner of man, so too they show the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge and kingship, and that He is the True King, exalted above creating it in vain and leaving it aimless after the perfection of its creation.

(Section: on His, glory be to Him, denial of those who claim that He did not create creation for any end or wisdom, such as His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose﴾

And His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left aimless?﴾ And His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth.﴾

The truth is the wisdom and the praiseworthy ends for which all of that was created, and these are many kinds: among them, that Allah, the Exalted, be known by His names, attributes, acts and signs; among them, that He be loved, worshipped, thanked, remembered and obeyed; among them, that He commands, forbids and legislates laws; among them, that He manages the affair, determines the decree and disposes of His dominion with various dispositions; among them, that He rewards and punishes, recompensing the doer of good for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, so that the effect of His justice and bounty is found, existent and witnessed, and He is praised and thanked for that; among them, that He makes His creatures know that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him; among them, that He honours the truthful and humiliates the liar; among them, the manifestation of the effects of His names and attributes, in their variety and multiplicity, in mental and external existence, so that His servants know that with knowledge corresponding to reality; among them, the testimony of all His creatures that He alone is their Lord, their Creator and their Sovereign, and that He alone is their God and their object of worship; among them, the manifestation of the effect of His sacred perfection, for creation and making are necessary to His perfection, since He is Living and Powerful, and whoever is so is only an acting, choosing agent; among them, that the effect of His wisdom appear in creatures by placing each of them in its fitting place, and by loving it in the manner which intellects and natural dispositions witness to be good, so that His dazzling wisdom is witnessed; among them, that He, glory be to Him, loves to be generous, to bestow, to pardon, to forgive and to overlook, and the necessary consequences of that must occur in creation and legislation; among them, that He loves to be praised, glorified, magnified, extolled and revered; among them, the abundance of the signs of His lordship, unity and divinity, and other wisdoms which creation includes. Thus He created His creatures by means of truth, for the sake of truth, and created them bound up with truth, and He Himself is truth; its source is truth, its end is truth, and it comprises truth. He has praised His believing servants in that they declared Him free of creating creation for no purpose or end, saying: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You."﴾ He informed that this is the supposition of His enemies, not of His allies, saying: ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the supposition of those who disbelieved.﴾

And how could one imagine that someone knew Him who says that He did not create for any wisdom sought by Him, and did not command for any wisdom, nor forbade for any wisdom, but that command and creation proceed only from pure will and power, not from wisdom nor any intended end? Is this not a denial of the reality of His praise? Rather, creation and command subsist only through wisdoms and ends; they are two manifestations of His praise and wisdom. So denying wisdom is denying the reality of His creation and command. For what the deniers affirm of that is what the Lord is exalted above, and He is too exalted to be attributed with it: they affirm a creation and a command with no mercy in it, no benefit and no wisdom, rather it is permissible for them, or occurs, that He commands what has no benefit whatsoever for the obligated person and forbids what has benefit, and all of that is equal in relation to Him.

It is permissible in their view that He commands everything He has forbidden and forbids everything He has commanded, and there is no difference between this and that except the mere command and prohibition. It is permissible in their view that He punish one who has not disobeyed Him for an instant, even though he spent his life in His obedience, thanks and remembrance, and that He bestow blessings upon one who has not obeyed Him for an instant, even though he spent his life in disbelief, polytheism, wrongdoing and wickedness. There is no way to know otherwise of Him except through the report of the Messenger; otherwise it is permissible for Him. This is among the worst and most evil suppositions about the Lord, the Exalted, and declaring Him free of it is like declaring Him free of wrongdoing and injustice. Indeed, this is the very wrongdoing from which Allah is exalted. The wondrous marvel is that many of the adherents of this doctrine declare Him free of what He described Himself with of attributes of perfection and majestic qualities, and claim that affirming them is anthropomorphism and likening; yet they do not declare Him free of this wrongdoing and injustice, and they claim that He is just and true, and that for them monotheism is not complete except by it, just as it is not complete except by denying His istiwa' (settling) over His Throne, His elevation above His heavens, His speech and His address, and the attributes of His perfection. Thus monotheism for this sect is not complete except by this negation and that affirmation. And Allah is the Guardian of success.

(Issue)

If it is said: What wisdom is there in causing pain to non-obligated animals?

We say: This is a question people have discussed, past and present, and their methods of answering it have differed. Those who deny the Chooser who acts by His will and power attribute that to bare nature, and say that it is among its necessary consequences and requirements, not the act of an agent, nor the power of one capable, nor the will of one willing.

Those who deny wisdom and causation refer that to pure will and the arbitrary choice that specifies, for example, one like another without a cause, without an end, without a sought wisdom, and without any reason at all. They thought that by this they would escape the question and close off for themselves the door of inquiry. Yet they only closed for themselves the door of knowing the Lord, His perfection, the perfection of His names, attributes and acts. Thus they nullified His wisdom, the reality of His divinity and His praise, and they were like those who seek refuge from the hot sand in the fire.

As for those who affirmed a wisdom and causation that return not to the Creator but to the creature, they followed the method of compensation for those pains with respect to those who will be raised for reward and punishment. They said: perhaps in that there is a reward for their patience and suffering, and a reward and compensation for them on the Day of Resurrection for the pains they endured. But then the causing of pain to animals, which are not rewarded or punished, was raised against them.

As for those who affirm the realities of the names and attributes of the Lord, and His wisdom, which is His description and for which He is called the Wise, and from which His creation and command proceed, they are the most knowledgeable of the sects regarding this matter, and their path in it is the soundest of paths and the safest from contradiction and confusion. For they combined the affirmation of power, general will and comprehensive wisdom, which is the end of the act, and they tied that to the names and attributes. Revelation, reason, the law and natural disposition thus corroborate one another among them, and they know that this is the requirement of perfect wisdom, that it is among its necessary consequences, that the necessary consequence of truth is truth, the necessary consequence of justice is justice, and the necessary consequences of wisdom are wisdom. Know, then, that here there are two matters:

...a soul moved by will and choice, and a nature moved without choice and will. Evil arises from these two moving things and from these two movements. This soul and this nature were created in this manner. This one moves toward its perfection, and that one moves toward its perfection. Good and evil arise from the two movements, just as good and evil arise from the movement of the celestial spheres, the sun and the moon, and from the movement of the winds, water, and fire.

The goods that arise from these movements are intended primarily, either for their own sake or because they are a means to greater goods than themselves. The evils that arise from them are not intended for their own sake, though they are intended as means and necessary concomitants that cannot be avoided. What the soul has been created with, of movement, is among the necessary attributes of its essence. The human soul is not a soul except with this necessary attribute.

If it is said: "Why were you created in constant motion?"

The answer is like saying: "Why was the soul a soul? Why was fire fire? Why was the wind wind?"

Had this not been created, it would not be a soul. Had the nature not been created in this way, it would not be a nature. Had the human being not been created with this attribute and this constitution, he would not be a human being.

[Chapter: On his ﷺ guidance in treating epilepsy (al-sar', seizure)]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both related, from the narration of ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Shall I show you a woman of the people of Paradise?" I said: "Yes." He said: "This black woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'I suffer from seizures, and I uncover myself, so pray to Allah for me.' He said: 'If you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise; and if you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you.' She said: 'I will be patient.' She said: 'But I uncover myself, so pray to Allah that I may not uncover myself.' So he prayed for her."

I say: Seizure is of two kinds: seizure from wicked earthly spirits, and seizure from corrupt humours.

The second is the one about which physicians speak regarding its cause and treatment.

As for seizure from spirits, it occurs through two matters: a matter from the side of the one afflicted, and a matter from the side of the treater. The matter from the side of the afflicted is through the strength of his soul, the sincerity of his turning toward the Originator and Creator of these spirits, and the sound seeking of refuge (taʿawwudh), in which the heart and tongue agree. This is a kind of combat, and the fighter cannot secure victory over his enemy with a weapon except through two things: that the weapon be sound and good in itself, and that the arm be strong. If either of these is lacking, the weapon profits little. How much more so when both are absent, when the heart is ruined of tawhid (monotheism), trust in Allah (tawakkul), piety, and turning to Him, and has no weapon.

The second is from the side of the treater, that he possesses these two matters as well. To the point that some treaters suffice with saying: "Come out of him," or "In the name of Allah," or "There is no power nor might except with Allah." The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Come out, enemy of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah."

I witnessed our shaykh send someone to the afflicted person to address the spirit within him, saying: "The shaykh says to you: Come out, for this is not lawful for you." Then the afflicted person would recover. Sometimes he addressed it himself. Sometimes the spirit was rebellious, so he would drive it out by striking, and the afflicted person would recover and feel no pain. We ourselves and others witnessed this from him many times.

He often recited into the ear of the afflicted person: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 115].

He related to me that he once recited it into the ear of the afflicted person, and the spirit said: "Yes," and he prolonged his voice with it.

He said: "So I took a stick and struck him with it on the veins of his neck until my hands grew weary from striking. The bystanders did not doubt that he would die from that beating. During the beating, she said: 'I love him.' I said to her: 'He does not love you.' She said: 'I want to perform Hajj with him.' I said to her: 'He does not want to perform Hajj with you.' She said: 'I will leave him out of respect for you.' I said: 'No, but out of obedience to Allah and His Messenger.' She said: 'Then I will come out of him.' He said: The afflicted man sat up, looking right and left, and said: 'What brought me to the presence of the shaykh?' They said to him: 'And all this beating?' He said: 'Why would the shaykh beat me when I have committed no sin?' And he did not perceive that any beating had fallen upon him at all."

He would treat with Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne), and he used to command the afflicted person and whoever treats him to recite it often, along with al-Muʿawwidhatayn (the two chapters of seeking refuge).

In sum, this kind of seizure and its treatment is denied only by one of little share of knowledge, intellect, and understanding. Most of the domination of wicked spirits over their people comes from the scarcity of their religion, the ruin of their hearts and tongues from the realities of remembrance (dhikr), the seeking of refuge (taʿawwudhat), and the Prophetic and faith-based protections. So the wicked spirit meets the man unarmed, with no weapon, and perhaps naked, and this affects him.

Had the veil been lifted, you would see most human souls stricken by these wicked spirits, held in their captivity and grip, which drive them wherever they wish, and they cannot refrain from them or oppose them. In them is the greatest seizure, from which their owner does not recover except at separation (death) and direct witnessing. Then he will realize that he was truly the one afflicted.

And from Allah is the help sought.

The treatment of this seizure is the union of sound intellect with faith in what the Messengers brought, and that Paradise and Hellfire be before his eyes and the direction of his heart; that he call to mind the people of this world, the descent of exemplary punishments and calamities upon them, and their falling within their dwellings like the falling of rain, while they are stricken and do not recover. How severe is the disease of this seizure! But when this affliction has become so widespread that none is seen except afflicted, it is no longer considered strange or reprehensible. Rather, because of the multitude of the afflicted, the strange and reprehensible thing has become its opposite.

So when Allah wills good for a servant, He awakens him from this seizure and looks at the sons of this world as afflicted around him, right and left, in their various classes. Among them is one whom madness has overwhelmed; among them is one who recovers briefly at times and returns to his madness; and among them is one who recovers once and goes mad another time. When he recovers, he acts as the people of recovery and intellect act, then the seizure returns to him and he falls into confusion.

He originates creation, then repeats it, that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

Now reflect on how the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them comprised truth at the beginning, the middle and the end; that they were created with truth, for truth, and bearing witness to truth. And He, the Exalted, rejected the one who supposed otherwise, saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾

Then He declared Himself free of this supposition, which contradicts His wisdom, knowledge and praise, saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the True King.﴾

Reflect on what is in these two names, "the True King," of refutation of this supposition which His enemies imagined, since it contradicts the perfection of His kingship and His being the Truth; for the True King is the one to whom command and prohibition belong, so He disposes of His creation by His word and command. This is the difference between "king" (malik) and "owner" (malik/mālik): the owner disposes by his action, and the king disposes by his action and command. The Lord, the Exalted, is the Owner of the kingdom, so He disposes by His action and command.

Whoever thinks that He created His creation in vain, not commanding them nor forbidding them, has impugned His kingship and has not esteemed Him with the esteem due to Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They did not esteem Allah with the esteem due to Him, when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being."﴾ Whoever denies the law of Allah, His command and His prohibition, and makes creation like grazing livestock, has impugned the kingship of Allah and has not esteemed Him with the esteem due to Him.

Likewise, His being the God of creation requires the perfection of His essence, attributes and names, and the occurrence of His acts in the most perfect and complete manner. Just as His essence is true, His speech is true, His promise is true, His command is true, and all His acts are true, and His recompense, which entails His law and religion, and the Last Day, is true; so whoever denies any of that has not described Allah as the Absolute Truth from every aspect and in every respect. For His being true entails His law, religion, reward and punishment. How, then, could one suppose of the True King that He would create His creation in vain, and leave them aimless, not commanding them, not forbidding them, not rewarding them, not punishing them? As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Does man think he will be left aimless?﴾

Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Neglected, not commanded and not forbidden."

Others said: "He is not recompensed for good and evil, nor rewarded, nor punished." The two statements are mutually implicative: al-Shafiʿi mentioned the cause of recompense, reward and punishment, which is command and prohibition, and the other mentioned the consequence of command and prohibition, which is the cause of recompense, reward and punishment.

Then reflect on His saying after that: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned.﴾ Whoever did not leave him, while a drop, aimless, but rather transformed the drop and turned it until it became more complete than it was, which is the clot; then transformed the clot until it became more complete than it was, until He created it and perfected its form, arranging it by His direction and wisdom through the stages of its perfections, until its perfection ended in a sound human being. How then would He leave him aimless, not driving him to the ultimate perfection for which he was created?

When the wise, discerning person contemplates the conditions of the drop from its origin to its end, it guides him to the Resurrection and the prophethoods, just as it guides him to the existence and oneness of the Creator and the attributes of His perfection. Just as the conditions of the drop from its beginning to its end show the perfection of the power of the Originator and Fashioner of man, so too they show the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge and kingship, and that He is the True King, exalted above creating it in vain and leaving it aimless after the perfection of its creation.

(Section: on His, glory be to Him, denial of those who claim that He did not create creation for any end or wisdom, such as His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose﴾

And His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left aimless?﴾ And His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth.﴾

The truth is the wisdom and the praiseworthy ends for which all of that was created, and these are many kinds: among them, that Allah, the Exalted, be known by His names, attributes, acts and signs; among them, that He be loved, worshipped, thanked, remembered and obeyed; among them, that He commands, forbids and legislates laws; among them, that He manages the affair, determines the decree and disposes of His dominion with various dispositions; among them, that He rewards and punishes, recompensing the doer of good for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, so that the effect of His justice and bounty is found, existent and witnessed, and He is praised and thanked for that; among them, that He makes His creatures know that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him; among them, that He honours the truthful and humiliates the liar; among them, the manifestation of the effects of His names and attributes, in their variety and multiplicity, in mental and external existence, so that His servants know that with knowledge corresponding to reality; among them, the testimony of all His creatures that He alone is their Lord, their Creator and their Sovereign, and that He alone is their God and their object of worship; among them, the manifestation of the effect of His sacred perfection, for creation and making are necessary to His perfection, since He is Living and Powerful, and whoever is so is only an acting, choosing agent; among them, that the effect of His wisdom appear in creatures by placing each of them in its fitting place, and by loving it in the manner which intellects and natural dispositions witness to be good, so that His dazzling wisdom is witnessed; among them, that He, glory be to Him, loves to be generous, to bestow, to pardon, to forgive and to overlook, and the necessary consequences of that must occur in creation and legislation; among them, that He loves to be praised, glorified, magnified, extolled and revered; among them, the abundance of the signs of His lordship, unity and divinity, and other wisdoms which creation includes. Thus He created His creatures by means of truth, for the sake of truth, and created them bound up with truth, and He Himself is truth; its source is truth, its end is truth, and it comprises truth. He has praised His believing servants in that they declared Him free of creating creation for no purpose or end, saying: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You."﴾ He informed that this is the supposition of His enemies, not of His allies, saying: ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the supposition of those who disbelieved.﴾

And how could one imagine that someone knew Him who says that He did not create for any wisdom sought by Him, and did not command for any wisdom, nor forbade for any wisdom, but that command and creation proceed only from pure will and power, not from wisdom nor any intended end? Is this not a denial of the reality of His praise? Rather, creation and command subsist only through wisdoms and ends; they are two manifestations of His praise and wisdom. So denying wisdom is denying the reality of His creation and command. For what the deniers affirm of that is what the Lord is exalted above, and He is too exalted to be attributed with it: they affirm a creation and a command with no mercy in it, no benefit and no wisdom, rather it is permissible for them, or occurs, that He commands what has no benefit whatsoever for the obligated person and forbids what has benefit, and all of that is equal in relation to Him.

It is permissible in their view that He commands everything He has forbidden and forbids everything He has commanded, and there is no difference between this and that except the mere command and prohibition. It is permissible in their view that He punish one who has not disobeyed Him for an instant, even though he spent his life in His obedience, thanks and remembrance, and that He bestow blessings upon one who has not obeyed Him for an instant, even though he spent his life in disbelief, polytheism, wrongdoing and wickedness. There is no way to know otherwise of Him except through the report of the Messenger; otherwise it is permissible for Him. This is among the worst and most evil suppositions about the Lord, the Exalted, and declaring Him free of it is like declaring Him free of wrongdoing and injustice. Indeed, this is the very wrongdoing from which Allah is exalted. The wondrous marvel is that many of the adherents of this doctrine declare Him free of what He described Himself with of attributes of perfection and majestic qualities, and claim that affirming them is anthropomorphism and likening; yet they do not declare Him free of this wrongdoing and injustice, and they claim that He is just and true, and that for them monotheism is not complete except by it, just as it is not complete except by denying His istiwa' (settling) over His Throne, His elevation above His heavens, His speech and His address, and the attributes of His perfection. Thus monotheism for this sect is not complete except by this negation and that affirmation. And Allah is the Guardian of success.

(Issue)

If it is said: What wisdom is there in causing pain to non-obligated animals?

We say: This is a question people have discussed, past and present, and their methods of answering it have differed. Those who deny the Chooser who acts by His will and power attribute that to bare nature, and say that it is among its necessary consequences and requirements, not the act of an agent, nor the power of one capable, nor the will of one willing.

Those who deny wisdom and causation refer that to pure will and the arbitrary choice that specifies, for example, one like another without a cause, without an end, without a sought wisdom, and without any reason at all. They thought that by this they would escape the question and close off for themselves the door of inquiry. Yet they only closed for themselves the door of knowing the Lord, His perfection, the perfection of His names, attributes and acts. Thus they nullified His wisdom, the reality of His divinity and His praise, and they were like those who seek refuge from the hot sand in the fire.

As for those who affirmed a wisdom and causation that return not to the Creator but to the creature, they followed the method of compensation for those pains with respect to those who will be raised for reward and punishment. They said: perhaps in that there is a reward for their patience and suffering, and a reward and compensation for them on the Day of Resurrection for the pains they endured. But then the causing of pain to animals, which are not rewarded or punished, was raised against them.

As for those who affirm the realities of the names and attributes of the Lord, and His wisdom, which is His description and for which He is called the Wise, and from which His creation and command proceed, they are the most knowledgeable of the sects regarding this matter, and their path in it is the soundest of paths and the safest from contradiction and confusion. For they combined the affirmation of power, general will and comprehensive wisdom, which is the end of the act, and they tied that to the names and attributes. Revelation, reason, the law and natural disposition thus corroborate one another among them, and they know that this is the requirement of perfect wisdom, that it is among its necessary consequences, that the necessary consequence of truth is truth, the necessary consequence of justice is justice, and the necessary consequences of wisdom are wisdom. Know, then, that here there are two matters:

...a soul moved by will and choice, and a nature moved without choice and will. Evil arises from these two moving things and from these two movements. This soul and this nature were created in this manner. This one moves toward its perfection, and that one moves toward its perfection. Good and evil arise from the two movements, just as good and evil arise from the movement of the celestial spheres, the sun and the moon, and from the movement of the winds, water, and fire.

The goods that arise from these movements are intended primarily, either for their own sake or because they are a means to greater goods than themselves. The evils that arise from them are not intended for their own sake, though they are intended as means and necessary concomitants that cannot be avoided. What the soul has been created with, of movement, is among the necessary attributes of its essence. The human soul is not a soul except with this necessary attribute.

If it is said: "Why were you created in constant motion?"

The answer is like saying: "Why was the soul a soul? Why was fire fire? Why was the wind wind?"

Had this not been created, it would not be a soul. Had the nature not been created in this way, it would not be a nature. Had the human being not been created with this attribute and this constitution, he would not be a human being.

[Chapter: On his ﷺ guidance in treating epilepsy (al-sar', seizure)]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both related, from the narration of ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Shall I show you a woman of the people of Paradise?" I said: "Yes." He said: "This black woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'I suffer from seizures, and I uncover myself, so pray to Allah for me.' He said: 'If you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise; and if you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you.' She said: 'I will be patient.' She said: 'But I uncover myself, so pray to Allah that I may not uncover myself.' So he prayed for her."

I say: Seizure is of two kinds: seizure from wicked earthly spirits, and seizure from corrupt humours.

The second is the one about which physicians speak regarding its cause and treatment.

As for seizure from spirits, it occurs through two matters: a matter from the side of the one afflicted, and a matter from the side of the treater. The matter from the side of the afflicted is through the strength of his soul, the sincerity of his turning toward the Originator and Creator of these spirits, and the sound seeking of refuge (taʿawwudh), in which the heart and tongue agree. This is a kind of combat, and the fighter cannot secure victory over his enemy with a weapon except through two things: that the weapon be sound and good in itself, and that the arm be strong. If either of these is lacking, the weapon profits little. How much more so when both are absent, when the heart is ruined of tawhid (monotheism), trust in Allah (tawakkul), piety, and turning to Him, and has no weapon.

The second is from the side of the treater, that he possesses these two matters as well. To the point that some treaters suffice with saying: "Come out of him," or "In the name of Allah," or "There is no power nor might except with Allah." The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Come out, enemy of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah."

I witnessed our shaykh send someone to the afflicted person to address the spirit within him, saying: "The shaykh says to you: Come out, for this is not lawful for you." Then the afflicted person would recover. Sometimes he addressed it himself. Sometimes the spirit was rebellious, so he would drive it out by striking, and the afflicted person would recover and feel no pain. We ourselves and others witnessed this from him many times.

He often recited into the ear of the afflicted person: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 115].

He related to me that he once recited it into the ear of the afflicted person, and the spirit said: "Yes," and he prolonged his voice with it.

He said: "So I took a stick and struck him with it on the veins of his neck until my hands grew weary from striking. The bystanders did not doubt that he would die from that beating. During the beating, she said: 'I love him.' I said to her: 'He does not love you.' She said: 'I want to perform Hajj with him.' I said to her: 'He does not want to perform Hajj with you.' She said: 'I will leave him out of respect for you.' I said: 'No, but out of obedience to Allah and His Messenger.' She said: 'Then I will come out of him.' He said: The afflicted man sat up, looking right and left, and said: 'What brought me to the presence of the shaykh?' They said to him: 'And all this beating?' He said: 'Why would the shaykh beat me when I have committed no sin?' And he did not perceive that any beating had fallen upon him at all."

He would treat with Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne), and he used to command the afflicted person and whoever treats him to recite it often, along with al-Muʿawwidhatayn (the two chapters of seeking refuge).

In sum, this kind of seizure and its treatment is denied only by one of little share of knowledge, intellect, and understanding. Most of the domination of wicked spirits over their people comes from the scarcity of their religion, the ruin of their hearts and tongues from the realities of remembrance (dhikr), the seeking of refuge (taʿawwudhat), and the Prophetic and faith-based protections. So the wicked spirit meets the man unarmed, with no weapon, and perhaps naked, and this affects him.

Had the veil been lifted, you would see most human souls stricken by these wicked spirits, held in their captivity and grip, which drive them wherever they wish, and they cannot refrain from them or oppose them. In them is the greatest seizure, from which their owner does not recover except at separation (death) and direct witnessing. Then he will realize that he was truly the one afflicted.

And from Allah is the help sought.

The treatment of this seizure is the union of sound intellect with faith in what the Messengers brought, and that Paradise and Hellfire be before his eyes and the direction of his heart; that he call to mind the people of this world, the descent of exemplary punishments and calamities upon them, and their falling within their dwellings like the falling of rain, while they are stricken and do not recover. How severe is the disease of this seizure! But when this affliction has become so widespread that none is seen except afflicted, it is no longer considered strange or reprehensible. Rather, because of the multitude of the afflicted, the strange and reprehensible thing has become its opposite.

So when Allah wills good for a servant, He awakens him from this seizure and looks at the sons of this world as afflicted around him, right and left, in their various classes. Among them is one whom madness has overwhelmed; among them is one who recovers briefly at times and returns to his madness; and among them is one who recovers once and goes mad another time. When he recovers, he acts as the people of recovery and intellect act, then the seizure returns to him and he falls into confusion.
